# @spellkave/player-mcp

> `PLAYER MCP gateway` — The hosted Remote MCP server for players (`mcp.spellkave.com`): an OAuth protected resource in front of the canonical PLAYER tool registry, with the public modding docs, public transcripts and world map tiles beside it.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `spellkave-player-mcp` | Start the gateway; the configuration is the environment (`SPELLKAVE_MCP_*`, `WORKOS_ISSUER`, `SPELLKAVE_WORLD_CATALOG`). Logs `spellkave-player-mcp: ready (trust-boundary=…)` and then one JSON operations line per request on stderr; SIGTERM stops it cleanly (through the tsx launcher the exit code is 143, bead sk-jay0.6.116). |
| `spellkave-player-mcp-health` | The container health check: exit 0 when `GET /healthz` answers 200, else 1. |
| `POST /mcp` | Stateless Streamable HTTP MCP (JSON-RPC in, one server-sent event out). Needs `Authorization: Bearer <AuthKit access token>`. |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/mcp]` | RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata: the issuer to log in at and the scopes. |
| `GET /healthz` | Readiness, redacted: `ok` or `unavailable`. |
| `GET /transcripts/<slug>` | A public world's transcript (JSONL), for logged-in spectators. |
| `GET /w/<slug>/…` | Map tiles, TileJSON, style and the OSM API 0.6 of a catalog world, for logged-in map clients from any origin. |

HTTP answers: `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge for a missing or untrusted token, `403` for an origin outside the allowlist, `404` for a route or world that does not exist (the Account API included: it is `api.spellkave.com`), `413`/`415` for a body a client should not send. The process exits `1` with the setting named on stderr when its configuration is refused.

How it answers and fails, with real records, is in [the guide](docs/guide.md#how-it-answers).

## What it promises

What `PLAYER MCP gateway` does is described and tested from the outside: 24 scenarios in [`behaviour/`](behaviour/) drive the real tool. The last run produced [`docs/guide.md`](docs/guide.md) (short, for people and agents) and [`docs/scenarios.md`](docs/scenarios.md) (every scenario with its transcripts).

Run: commit `066659388d + local changes`, 2026-10-30T18:19Z, full suite — 40 verified.

- **[How the PLAYER MCP gateway answers](docs/scenarios.md#how-the-player-mcp-gateway-answers)** — 2 scenarios
  - An MCP answer is one JSON-RPC message in a server-sent event.
  - A configuration the deployment contract forbids stops the gateway before it listens.
- **[Log in to the PLAYER MCP gateway](docs/scenarios.md#log-in-to-the-player-mcp-gateway)** — 7 scenarios
  - A token the gateway cannot trust is refused with 401 invalid_token.
- **[Start playing through the MCP tools](docs/scenarios.md#start-playing-through-the-mcp-tools)** — 4 scenarios
  - A call the gateway can refuse by itself never reaches a world.
- **[Call the gateway from a browser](docs/scenarios.md#call-the-gateway-from-a-browser)** — 7 scenarios
  - A request a trusted page would not send is refused before it is read.
  - Public transcripts are for logged-in spectators of public worlds.
  - Map clients from any origin are challenged, and unknown worlds do not exist.
- **[Run and watch the gateway](docs/scenarios.md#run-and-watch-the-gateway)** — 4 scenarios

## Behaviour suite

From [`vitest.behaviour.config.ts`](vitest.behaviour.config.ts):

Behaviour suite: Gherkin scenarios in behaviour/*.feature start the real
PLAYER MCP gateway (bundled once by behaviour/support/setup.ts) against a
fake issuer on 127.0.0.1, one of each per scenario, and talk to it with
curl; nothing under `src/` is imported. Scenarios share nothing (own ports,
own temp dir), so feature files run in parallel. Offline: no world, no
deployment, no credential, no outside network. The default `vitest run`
does not pick it up; scripts/ci/run-ci-js.sh runs it as its own step.

`pnpm guide` (`behaviour-docs guide`, from @spellkave/behaviour) turns the
last run into docs/guide.md and docs/scenarios.md.

From [`behaviour/steps.ts`](behaviour/steps.ts):

The sentences of behaviour/*.feature. Each scenario starts the real PLAYER
MCP gateway (support/gateway.ts: the runtime bundled once by
support/setup.ts, or bin/spellkave-player-mcp.js for @launcher) against its
own fake issuer (support/fake-issuer.ts), and talks to it the way a client
does: one `curl` per request, whose transcript is attached to the report.
Nothing under src/ is imported. The roster sentences read the canonical
PLAYER contracts from @spellkave/tool-contracts, the source the gateway
projects; that is the contract under test, not a copy of it.

curl runs with `-q` (no ~/.curlrc) and an environment of PATH only, so no
proxy or config of the developer's shell sits between curl and the gateway.

From [`behaviour/support/gateway.ts`](behaviour/support/gateway.ts):

One PLAYER MCP gateway per scenario, started the way a deployment starts it:
the real runtime entry (src/runtime-main.ts, bundled once by setup.ts, or
the real bin/spellkave-player-mcp.js for the @launcher scenario) with its
configuration in the environment and nothing else. The scenario talks to it
only over HTTP (curl, steps.ts) and reads only what it answers and logs.

The world it points at:
- WORKOS_ISSUER is a fake issuer (fake-issuer.ts) on its own port;
- SPELLKAVE_MCP_WORLD_URL is a closed port, so every seat probe fails at
  once and every player is a player without a hero (a seat needs a live
  SpacetimeDB subscription, which no offline fake can answer);
- the catalog holds one public world `elven-mini-1` and one private world
  `private-1`; the public one has a transcript on disk.
The listen port is ephemeral, which runtime.ts allows only for a loopback
canonical origin. Trust boundary `network-policy` lets the world URL point
at the closed port instead of the fixed 127.0.0.1:3000, where a developer's
own local node may be listening.

The environment is built from scratch: no SPELLKAVE_*, WORKOS_*, OTEL_* or
XDG_* of the developer's shell reaches the gateway, and HOME is the
scenario's temp dir, so no local cli.toml or state file is read or written.

From [`behaviour/support/fake-issuer.ts`](behaviour/support/fake-issuer.ts):

A fake WorkOS AuthKit issuer for behaviour scenarios: an HTTP server on an
ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port that publishes a JWKS at `/oauth2/jwks` (the path
the gateway derives from `WORKOS_ISSUER`) and signs access tokens with the
matching private key. The gateway under test never reaches the real
AuthKit; it checks these tokens with its own production verifier.

Plain HTTP is enough: the gateway accepts any issuer URL and fetches the
JWKS with `fetch`, unlike the refresh grant that gateway-identity's
`fake-authkit.ts` fakes over HTTPS. The shape follows that fake on purpose
(`startFake…()` -> `{ issuer, requests, close() }`), and the Account API
suite builds a similar fake issuer in `packages/spellkave-api`; once both
exist, one shared helper in `@spellkave/behaviour` can replace them.

A generated public key under an example issuer provides the reference
shape. Each scenario signs with its own ephemeral key. The fake serves
only public JWK members; the verifier imports the key from kty, n and e.

## Unit tests

A unit test stays only for what the behaviour suite cannot reach. The line above each test says why (`// keep(K…): …`, or one `// keep-file(K…): …` line for a whole file), or names the scenario it still lacks (`// open: …`).

- **K1** one of several cases over a pure function
- **K2** a branch the public surface cannot provoke without an injected host, process, fault or TTY
- **K3** a cross-run invariant (determinism, idempotence, ordering)
- **K4** a compile proof, snapshot or documentation drift gate
- **K5** a contract with another tool the suite does not drive (shell scripts, shared file formats)
